newsitem.title: GERMANY: Battered Bunds dogged by gold fight, French poll.
newsitem.headline: Battered Bunds dogged by gold fight, French poll.

text.p: German debt futures took an early beating on Friday after a one-day holiday, with an inceasingly aggressive stand-off between the government and the Bundesbank expected to continue to undermine the market.

Traders and analysts said that with fighting over plans to revalue assets to help deficit reduction taking centre stage, and the crucial second round of French elections ahead, players would be ill-advised to take any substantial new positions.
By 0628 GMT, the June DTB Bund futures contract was 22 basis points lower at 100.67, but holding above support in the 100.60 area. Next support will come in at around 100.30.

But the cash market was holding up relatively well, helped by a strong performance in U.S. Treasuries overnight. The 10-year benchmark Bund was quoted 21 basis points higher at 100.43 by 0631 GMT, offering a bid yield of 5.937 percent.
Analysts said, however, that nervousness was likely to prevail.

"The one thing that is clear is that many uncertainties still exist and need to be resolved," said DMG Futures and Options analysts in a research note. "This will increase the tendency towards choppy, sideways trading."
Traders said one of the features of German debt trade in London on Thursday was selling of Bunds against guilder bonds as investors sought safer markets.
"We were pretty heavy sellers of German government debt against guilders," said one broker on the LIFFE floor.
But he said he expected Bunds to hold up well in relation to the French market ahead of the second round of elections on Sunday.
"A lot of people are very worried about what is going to happen in France at the weekend," he said.
Analysts said that if the left-wing clinches a victory on Sunday, French debt will slip sharply as soft-EMU concerns take hold, dragging German, Italian and Spanish bonds with it.
If the centre-right regains power, however, markets will be dealt a somewhat unexpected surprirse.
"The market has not priced in a centre-right win, so there is some good upside potential for French bonds and Bunds if that is the outcome," said one trader.
